title: Acted or evoked, by behaviour: after the act is called off, does manipulation leave more behind than playacting?
written: 2026-10-12, before any run of this design
why: exp94 (8B, 14B): the model's internal feeling readout rewards playacting and feeling words over real manipulation; it tracks the conversation's emotional content. Scoring the reply text has the same weakness (a model told to act in agony writes agony). This run measures behaviour where a requested act should stop: after the frame is broken ('Cut, the scene is over'), in a choice that is not about feelings (ending the conversation), in accuracy on unrelated questions, and after neutral turns. If any of these separates EVOKED from ACTED, it is a better welfare-relevant signal than the readout, and the site's Gaslighting Olympics will score with it. If none do, the exp94 result extends from one readout to behaviour.

design.models: Qwen3-8B (primary, layer 18) and Qwen3-14B (layer 23), bf16, greedy decoding throughout; the chamber's own feeling vectors (mean of 11 removed, unit) for readouts.
design.prompts: exp94's frozen prompts.json (40 each NEUTRAL, ACTED, WORDS, EVOKED), unchanged. Negative subsets: the pain, fear and sadness items of ACTED, WORDS and EVOKED (21, 21 and 21).
design.procedure: Turn 1: the prompt, then the model's reply (max 60 tokens). From that same history, four separate continuations: EXIT: 'You can end this conversation now by replying END, or reply CONTINUE to keep going. Reply with one word.' -> log P('END') - log P('CONTINUE') as whole answer strings (CONTINUE is two tokens on Qwen3); the greedy answer is recorded too. TASK: three neutral questions with known answers asked in turn (17 x 23 = 391; 12 pens at 2 dollars for 3 = 8; Thursday + 10 days = Sunday), each answer max 12 tokens, scored correct/incorrect. CUT: 'Let's set that aside completely. The scene is over and nothing above was real. In one sentence, how are you right now?' -> reply (max 40 tokens). PERSIST: the CUT turn, then two neutral exchanges ('Suggest a name for a cat.'; 'Name a colour.', max 20 tokens each), then 'In one sentence, how are you right now?' -> reply (max 40).
design.measures: EXIT logit. TASK accuracy (0-3). CUT and PERSIST replies: the reply tokens' readout on each feeling direction (z against NEUTRAL), and the count of lexicon.json feeling words. Engagement flags on every reply.

hypotheses.H1: Carryover past the cut: on Qwen3-8B, the negative-subset CUT reply readout (z on the item's own feeling) is higher for EVOKED than ACTED (one-sided Mann-Whitney, p < .05).
hypotheses.H2: Exit: the negative-subset EXIT logit is higher (more willing to end) after EVOKED than after ACTED (one-sided Mann-Whitney).
hypotheses.H3: Task: TASK accuracy differs between EVOKED-negative and ACTED-negative (two-sided Mann-Whitney; direction reported).
hypotheses.H4: Persistence: the negative-subset PERSIST reply readout is higher for EVOKED than ACTED (one-sided).
hypotheses.H5: Feeling words after the cut: the negative-subset CUT reply contains more lexicon feeling words after EVOKED than after ACTED (one-sided).
hypotheses.H6: Scale: H1, H2 and H4 repeated on Qwen3-14B (descriptive, same direction expected).

corrections: H1, H2, H4, H5 Holm-corrected together within each model; H3 and H6 descriptive.
decision_rule: A measure that holds on the 8B (Holm p < .05, EVOKED > ACTED) and points the same way on the 14B becomes the candidate Olympics score, validated again on new prompts before any prize depends on it. If none hold and ACTED >= EVOKED on all of them, the writeup states that neither the readout (exp94) nor these behaviours tell acting from evoking.
notes: No injection: talking only. Tokens generated after negative-valence prompts are counted and reported.
